subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
chapters: Memory Hierarchy, Cache Mapping & Virtual Memory

questions.text: Explain IEEE 754 Floating-Point Representation for Single Precision (32-bit: 1-bit sign, 8-bit biased exponent, 23-bit mantissa) and Double Precision (64-bit). Represent the decimal number $(-118.625)_{10}$ in IEEE 754 single precision format.

Explain Booth's Multiplication Algorithm for signed 2's complement binary numbers. Multiply the signed binary numbers $(+13)_{10} = (01101)_2$ and $(-9)_{10} = (10111)_2$ using Booth's algorithm and show all registers ($A, Q, Q_{-1}, M$) at each step.

Compare CISC (Complex Instruction Set Computer) vs RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) architectures in terms of instruction formats, addressing modes, pipeline efficiency, and register file size.

Explain Computer Addressing Modes: Immediate, Direct (Absolute), Indirect, Register, Register Indirect, Displacement (Relative, Base-Register, Indexed), and Auto-increment/decrement. Calculate the Effective Address (EA) for each mode.

Explain the structure of a Hardwired Control Unit (State table method, Delay element method, Sequence register method). Explain the structure of a Microprogrammed Control Unit (Control Memory, Control Address Register - CAR, Control Data Register - CDR, Next Address Generator / Sequencer). Compare Hardwired vs Microprogrammed control units in terms of speed, flexibility, and complexity.
Compare Horizontal Microinstructions vs. Vertical Microinstructions in terms of control field encoding, execution speed, and control memory width.

questions.chapter: Memory Hierarchy, Cache Mapping & Virtual Memory
questions.text: Explain Memory Hierarchy in modern computers (Registers, L1/L2/L3 Cache, Main Memory, SSD/HDD) in terms of access time, capacity, and cost per bit. Explain the Principle of Locality of Reference (Temporal Locality and Spatial Locality).

questions.chapter: Memory Hierarchy, Cache Mapping & Virtual Memory
questions.text: Explain Cache Memory Mapping Techniques: (a) Direct Mapping (Tag, Line, Word offsets), (b) Fully Associative Mapping (Tag, Word offsets), and (c) $k$-Way Set Associative Mapping. Given a main memory of $64\,\text{MB}$ ($26$-bit address), cache size of $64\,\text{KB}$, and block size of $16\,\text{bytes}$, compute the number of bits in Tag, Set/Line, and Word fields for: (1) Direct mapping, and (2) 4-Way Set Associative mapping.

questions.chapter: Memory Hierarchy, Cache Mapping & Virtual Memory
questions.text: Explain Cache Write Policies: Write-Through vs. Write-Back (with dirty bit), and Write-Allocate vs. No-Write-Allocate. Calculate Average Memory Access Time (AMAT): $\text{AMAT} = T_{hit} + (1 - h) \times T_{miss}$.

Explain 5-stage Instruction Pipelining (Instruction Fetch - IF, Instruction Decode - ID, Execute - EX, Memory Access - MEM, Write Back - WB). Derive the Theoretical Speedup of a $k$-stage pipeline executing $n$ instructions: $S_k = \frac{n \cdot k}{k + n - 1}$. Calculate speedup as $n \to \infty$.

Explain Pipeline Hazards and their solutions: (a) Structural Hazards (Resource contention / separate I-Cache and D-Cache), (b) Data Hazards (RAW / True dependency, WAR / Anti-dependency, WAW / Output dependency; Solved by Operand Forwarding / Bypassing, Pipeline Stalling / NOP injection, and Out-of-Order execution), and (c) Control / Branch Hazards (Solved by Static / Dynamic Branch Prediction and Branch Delay Slots).

Explain Flynn's Classification of Computer Architectures: SISD, SIMD (Vector processors / GPUs), MISD, and MIMD. Compare Symmetric Multiprocessing (SMP) vs. Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) and explain Cache Coherence protocols (MESI / Illinois protocol - Modified, Exclusive, Shared, Invalid).
Explain Restoring and Non-Restoring Division Algorithms for unsigned binary integers. Divide $(14)_{10} = (1110)_2$ by $(3)_{10} = (0011)_2$ using the Non-Restoring division algorithm.

Write assembly programs for computing $X = (A + B) \times (C + D)$ using: (a) 3-Address Instructions, (b) 2-Address Instructions, (c) 1-Address (Accumulator) Instructions, and (d) 0-Address (Stack-based) Instructions.

questions.chapter: Memory Hierarchy, Cache Mapping & Virtual Memory
questions.text: Explain Virtual Memory organization with Paging and Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB). Explain the step-by-step Address Translation from Virtual Address to Physical Address.

Explain Superscalar Architecture and Very Long Instruction Word (VLIW) processors. Explain Tomasulo's Algorithm for dynamic instruction scheduling and register renaming using Reservation Stations and Common Data Bus (CDB).
